title: Rational sections with support preserve finite-constant-model bounded constructibility
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$; all schemes are separated of finite type over $k$ and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in it. Let $\Lambda=E$, with the condensed ring $S\mapsto C(S,E)$ of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], or $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with the condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed] whose sections on a profinite set $S$ are the continuous maps $S\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with image in some finite subextension; pull it back to $\Lambda_T$ on the small pro-étale site of each scheme $T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For such $T$ let $\Dbc(T,\Lambda)\subset D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ be the full subcategory of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: bounded complexes of $\Lambda_T$-modules each of whose cohomology sheaves admits a finite stratification of $T$ by constructible locally closed subschemes on each of which it has a finite constant local model (pro-étale locally of the form $\Lambda\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P$ with $P$ a finitely presented $\Lambda(*)$-module).

Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of such schemes, and let $R\underline\Gamma_Z:D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ be the derived functor of sections with support in $Z$ of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support]. Then for every $K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ one has $R\underline\Gamma_ZK\in\Dbc(Z,\Lambda)$.

source.place: last clause '$R\underline\Gamma_ZK\in\Dbc(Z,\Lambda)$', with $\Dbc$ read in the finite-constant-local-model convention of sk-def-sfb-constructible used by sk-prop-sf-existence and sk-thm-restriction (the existing DAG node det-prop-closed-adjoint-constructible-support states it for the convention of sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible)

proof.text: The standing setting makes $X$ and $Z$ finite type over the field $k$. Every ideal in a field is either zero or the whole field, hence finitely generated. The one affine chart of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is therefore Noetherian and its underlying singleton space is quasi-compact; thus $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a Noetherian scheme. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes both $X$ and $Z$ Noetherian. In particular $X$ is quasi-separated, since a locally Noetherian scheme is [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the open immersion of the complement $U=X\setminus Z$. Then $U$ is Noetherian and therefore quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] to $U\to X$ shows that $j$ is quasi-compact. Thus the hypotheses of the open direct-image and closed-support inputs apply.

source.place: first paragraph: Noetherian standing-scheme case and quasi-compact complement

proof.text: For $f=j$ or $f=i$, the coefficient identification and exact module inverse image are given by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Pull a finite stratification back along $f$ using [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification]. Pull back its pro-étale local covers as well. On each such cover, [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model] writes the module as the cokernel of a finite scalar matrix $A$. The exact inverse image preserves that cokernel and the finite free source and target; the coefficient identification carries $A$ to the same scalar matrix, giving the required finite constant local model on the inverse-image stratum. Exactness preserves kernels and cokernels [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], hence also $H^q=\ker d^q/\operatorname{im}d^{q-1}$. The exact derived inverse image is computed termwise by [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], so its cohomology is $f^*H^q$ and remains zero outside the original finite interval. This proves that $j^*$ and $i^*$ preserve the finite-constant-model bounded constructible category.

source.place: second paragraph: restriction and pullback preserve constructibility

proof.text:
Apply clause (3) of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived] to $i$ and its open complement $j$. It gives, without any constructibility assumption, the distinguished triangle
$$i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K\longrightarrow(i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK)[1]$$
in the ambient derived category, with second arrow the unit of $j^*\dashv Rj_*$. In particular $F:=i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK$ is the fiber of that unit map. Only this formal triangle is used here; its statement imposes no choice between the two constructibility conventions.

source.place: first paragraph: the derived closed-support localization triangle

proof.text: By step 2, $j^*K\in\Dbc(U,\Lambda)$. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-open-direct-image-constructible] to the quasi-compact open immersion $j$ of step 1. Its conclusion gives $Rj_*j^*K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ in the finite-constant-local-model convention, for both $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.

source.place: second paragraph: restriction and open direct-image finiteness

proof.text: The middle term $K$ is in $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ by hypothesis, and the third term is in that category by step 4. The finite-constant-model bounded constructible category is triangulated and closed under isomorphisms by [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-triangulated]. Applying its two-out-of-three property to the triangle in step 3 yields $F:=i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$; its shift $F[1]$ is also in $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$.

source.place: second paragraph: triangulated closure of the localization triangle

proof.text: The fiber formula in [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived] identifies $R\underline\Gamma_ZK$ with $i^*F$, because $F$ is the fiber of the unit map $K\to Rj_*j^*K$ in the triangle of step 3. The scheme $Z$ is Noetherian by step 1. Applying the exact pullback preservation argument of step 2 to $i$ gives $i^*F\in\Dbc(Z,\Lambda)$, and closure under isomorphisms in [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-triangulated] transfers this membership across the fiber-formula isomorphism. Therefore $R\underline\Gamma_ZK\in\Dbc(Z,\Lambda)$, while step 5 already gives all three displayed terms and the shift in $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$.

source.place: second paragraph, last sentence: recover supported complex by closed pullback and fiber formula

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs: localization triangle, open direct-image finiteness, triangulated closure, and closed inverse image; expanded for the finite constant local model convention
